messages:
aisha: Quick mini-audit on a couple of incoming model onboarding PRs — want to make sure config.json checks are sane before we flip the gate. I ran the validator locally and hit a few small things. Posting a short checklist and callouts.

Checklist: 1) weights S3 path reachable + checksummed; 2) tokenizer special_token ids match serving defaults (pad/eos/unk); 3) max_seq_length present and <= runtime hard limit; 4) dtype/quant profile (float16/int8) explicitly set or has a clear fallback; 5) no deprecated fields (vocab_path vs tokenizer.vocab).

Can owners please confirm for models in PRs #4123 and #4131?

sophie: For #4123 the tokenizer has a weird extra special token id. The config has "tokenizer": { "pad_token_id": 0, "eos_token_id": 50257 } but the tokenizer files expect eos=2. Found this when running tokenization sanity: it tokenizes <|endoftext|> as id 2. :eyes:

I ran: ```python
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
tok = Tokenizer.from_file('s3://redwood-models/m/foo/tokenizer.json')
print(tok.token_to_id('<|endoftext|>'))
```

raj: I moved weights for #4131 earlier today — new path is s3://redwood-models/dedicated/multi/4131/v1/weights.pt (sha256: 9f2b...). Updated the PR description but forgot to update config.json. I'll open a small patch to point the weights_uri field to that path. CI had a checksum mismatch earlier.

ci-bot: build/validator — 1954321205 — FAIL — model-config-validator — PR #4131 — checksum mismatch for weights_uri (expected 9f2b..., found none). See logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/3123/logs

max: For the tokenizer mismatch Sophie mentioned, we should add a non-fatal warning in the validator that flags mismatched special token ids and suggests mapping. Production serving should fall back to the tokenizer's native ids if config disagrees, but surface the diff in console and dashboard. Example small jq check to spot discrepant fields in a config bundle: ```bash
jq '.tokenizer | {pad_token_id, eos_token_id, unk_token_id}' config.json
```

Also: we need a lightweight deprecation detector for configs. Common culprit: old teams still use "vocab_path" at top level instead of "tokenizer.vocab_path". Suggest a linter rule that maps known deprecated keys to new ones and fails only if both are missing.

elaine: Who wants to own the schema+validator PR? I can toggle the canary rollout after we merge. We should also add a one-liner to the onboarding docs so SREs know how to hotfix in prod if validator blocks an urgent rollout. Link to docs draft: https://redwood-infra/docs/onboarding/config#schema (internal)

raj: I'll submit the patch updating weights_uri in #4131 in ~15m. Also adding the checksum file alongside weights.

sophie: I'll open a tiny PR that updates the tokenizer fields to match actual tokenizer file for #4123 (pad=0, eos=2). I'll add a note in the PR explaining the mismatch and the jq sanity check.

max: I'll start the validator/deprecation detector branch, will push a prototype by EOD. Plan: add non-fatal "warnings" output, a failing error for missing required keys (weights_uri, tokenizer.*.json, max_seq_length), and mapping table for deprecated keys.

aisha: Awesome. Can we agree owners: raj -> weights path fixes, sophie -> tokenizer config fixes, max -> validator changes, elaine -> canary/rollout? If so I'll update the onboarding checklist in the PR template. :thumbsup:

elaine: works for me.

ci-bot: build/validator — 1954321378 — WARN — schema-lint — PR #4123 — tokenizer ids mismatch (config.eos=50257 vs tokenizer.eos=2) — warning emitted to PR checks.

aisha: Thanks everyone — ping me if anything blocks merge. I'll add the checklist entry to the PR template and a very short rollback playbook (replace weights_uri with previous release and revert canary).
